title: Is merger enforcement too lax? Bhattacharya, Illanes & Stillerman (AER 2026)
description:
Across a broad sample of consumer packaged goods mergers the average price effect is near zero but the spread is wide. What that means for the claim that antitrust enforcement has been lax, and what an enforcement model says would happen under a stricter standard.

Paper: Bhattacharya, V., Illanes, G., and Stillerman, D. (2026). Merger Effects and Antitrust Enforcement: Evidence from US Consumer Packaged Goods. American Economic Review 116(8), 2996-3035. DOI 10.1257/aer.20240497.

Link: https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20240497

Sources the script was based on: the open NBER working paper 31123 (revision of August 2025), essentially the full text (main text, conclusion, most appendices), read via automated extraction; the published AER version was not read

Caveats: Every figure comes from the working-paper version and may differ from the published AER version. Ranges such as the average price effect and the counterfactual price declines depend on specification, so the episode gives them approximately. The authors' enforcement thresholds are estimated from only ten challenged mergers. Not covered in the text read: whether pack-size changes are handled.

title: Collusion by exclusion: how a bid-rigging cartel can exploit preselection (Seibel & Škoda, AEJ Micro 2026)
description:
A theory of how a partial bid-rigging cartel can use bidder preselection to shut out competitive rivals, a collusion marker built from near-identical opening bids, and what happened in Slovak public procurement when the preselection stage was removed in 2017.

Paper: Seibel, R. and Škoda, S. (2026). Collusion by Exclusion in Public Procurement. American Economic Journal: Microeconomics 18(3), 148-202. DOI 10.1257/mic.20240308.

Link: https://doi.org/10.1257/mic.20240308

Sources the script was based on: the author-hosted PDF dated August 2025 on Samuel Škoda's website, essentially the full text (main text, conclusion, most appendix discussion), read via automated extraction in two passes; the published AEJ Micro version was not read

Caveats: All figures come from the August 2025 author version and may differ from the published article. The extraction showed small inconsistencies between the text and tables, for example the reform effect on cartel members facing each other, so those numbers are given as ranges. The convicted-cartel validation rests on one case of six firms and 274 auctions in the data. The 2017 reform bundled preselection removal with other rule changes. The euro counterfactuals are illustrative. Not covered: the published version's revisions, the extension appendices in detail.
